summary.tldr: The bill limits replacement workers in federal labour disputes, adds penalties, and speeds up decisions on work that must continue during strikes or lockouts.
what_it_does: Expands the federal ban on replacement workers during legal strikes and lockouts, and bars use of certain contractors, transferred workers, volunteers, students and members of the public.
Prohibits employers, during a strike or lockout meant to stop work by all employees in a bargaining unit, from using employees in that unit for other work, except in limited cases.
Allows replacement services only for urgent situations involving an imminent or serious threat to life, safety, property or serious environmental damage, if no other means are available.
Creates an offence for breaking these rules, with fines of up to $100,000 for each day the offence continues, and lets the government set administrative monetary penalties by regulation.
Requires employers and unions to try to agree on work that must continue within 15 days after notice to bargain, or have the Canada Industrial Relations Board decide.
Sets timelines for the Board to decide maintenance of activities cases, and requires reinstating striking or locked-out employees before other people when a stoppage ends.
summary.background: The bill changes rules in the Canada Labour Code for legal strikes and lockouts in federally regulated workplaces. It also amends the Canada Industrial Relations Board Regulations, 2012.
